title: Cost counts every archived execution
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/cost.rs (041's cost step `record`, `/api/cost`'s `window`, and the prices), crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`spawn_cost_messages` and `spawn_cost_record`: one row per assistant message, folded from the Bridge's `model.usage` events, priced when recorded) and crates/spawn-postgres/src/cost.rs; crates/spawn-host/src/transcripts.rs and docs/storage.md "Transcript archive" (`<workspace root>/.transcripts/<agent>/<native>.jsonl` is copy 0 of a native session's transcript, `<native>.<n>.jsonl` copy n); crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/transcripts.rs (how the scorecard already reads that archive: one message once per id across every line and copy); crates/spawn-cli/src/commands/loops.rs (the loop's steps); web/src/cost.ts and web/src/components/cost/CostView.tsx (the Cost page).

The problem. Objective 041 counts a model call only when the Bridge emits a `model.usage` event as it reads a transcript. Every execution that ended before that Bridge ran was read without them, so its calls are in the transcript archive and in no cost. On the live fleet on 2026-11-11, `/api/cost?window=24h` and `?window=7d` gave the same $109.71, while the archive's last 24 h held about $168.9 of calls, from 13 more workers. The Cost page's "Last 7 days" read about 35% low and said nothing about it. Any future gap (a usage event lost, an execution read by an older Bridge) would be just as silent.

Required behaviour. (a) The loop counts, without a person, every assistant message the transcript archive holds and the cost record lacks. It does so each time it starts (every deploy restarts it); running it again adds nothing. It counts by 041's rules: once per `message.id` across every line and every copy file, with the largest usage of its lines, at its earliest line's `timestamp`, under that line's `message.model`, priced by SPAWN_MODEL_PRICES when it is recorded (a model with no price counts its tokens unpriced). It counts for the agent whose archive directory holds it, that agent's execution running at the message's time (the latest one started at or before it; for a message timed before all of them, the agent's first), the task the agent held then (041's rule: its latest task assigned at or before the message's time; for a message timed before any task, the latest assigned at or before that execution started; none: no task), and that task's mission. A message the record already holds keeps what it holds. Each message counts, not each execution: an execution whose later messages were recorded but whose earlier ones were not gets its earlier ones counted. An archived message of an agent with no recorded execution is not counted, and the loop's log says how many such messages it skipped. A message counted from the archive and later read by the Bridge is still one message.

(b) `GET /api/cost` (both windows) answers `counted_since_ms`, the time (ms since the epoch) of the earliest message the cost record holds, or null when it holds none. web/src/cost.ts's `costView(answer)` gains `since`: "Counted since <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> UTC" (that time, to the minute, in UTC) when the answer's `since_ms` is before `counted_since_ms`, and null otherwise (no message counted, or the window starts at or after it). The Cost page shows it on each window it applies to, so a figure that covers part of its window never reads as the whole. cost.ts and everything it imports must load with node alone: type stripping, no bundler, no packages, relative imports naming their `.ts` file, `import type` for anything used only as a type, and only erasable TypeScript (no enum, namespace or parameter property).

(c) Read only the archive: never the engine's live transcripts under SPAWN_CLAUDE_PROJECTS, and never the database's events as a second source. A file that cannot be read, or a line that is not JSON, is skipped and the rest is counted. The work on each start is bounded by what the archive holds (the live archive is about 0.5 GB). A restart must not re-read unchanged files in full when nothing is missing: keep what was counted per file (its length or a digest) in the database, or check cheaply before reading. The count never holds up the loop's other steps: recovery after a host restart, delivery, the dispatcher and the alerts run on their usual passes while it works, so a deploy or reboot with the live archive delays none of them (028 (8) and 044 expect a resume within 20 s of the loop's start). It works in bounded pieces, a bounded number of files or bytes per pass, resuming where it left off, or beside the passes, never in one pass of the whole archive. It sends bounded batches to the store, never every message in one call. An error in one piece (an unreadable file, a store call that fails) is said in the loop's log and skips or retries that piece alone; it never restarts the whole count.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/048.sh, run against a tree, makes history as the live fleet has it. Two workers report and their executions end. Then, with the loop stopped, the scenario deletes in its own database every `model.usage` event of one worker and the event for the first message of the other, along with their rows in the cost record, and leaves the archive alone.
- With serve alone, the answer is the kept use, and `counted_since_ms` is the earliest kept message.
- Within 30 s of the loop starting, the 24 h and 7 d totals, every mission, task, agent and execution, and `counted_since_ms` are what the archive holds, and each agent's 7 d tokens equal a recount of the archive over the answer's window. A message from 11 days back counts in neither window, and messages timed before a worker's task count for that task.
- A live worker after that counts once.
- A second copy of an archived transcript and two restarts of the loop change no figure.
- `costView`'s `since` reads the minute before the history is counted and null after.

The product reason. The owner sees what the fleet costs over 7 days and can trust the number: every model call the archive holds is in it, counted once, and a figure that covers only part of its window says so.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
